newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-SABRES GOALIE HASEK SUSPENDED THREE GAMES FOR ALTERCATION.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-SABRES GOALIE HASEK SUSPENDED THREE GAMES FOR ALTERCATION.

text.p: NEW YORK, May 1 (Reuter) Buffalo Sabres star goaltender Dominik Hasek was suspended for three playoff games and fined $10,000 by the NHL Thursday for grabbing a reporter who had written a critical story about him.

Hasek, enraged by a column written by Jim Kelley of the Buffalo News, confronted Kelley outside the Sabres locker room after Saturday's Game Five of the Eastern Conference series against the Ottawa Senators, grabbed him and ripped his shirt.
Hasek missed the final four games of the series with a sprained right knee, an injury which Kelley suggested in print was not as serious as announced.

Hasek will be suspended for the first three games of the series against the Philadelphia Flyers, although there had been no word on whether he would have been fit to play. Backup Steve Shields has been starting in his place.

"There is no dispute that Mr. Hasek had physical contact with Mr. Kelley," NHL commissioner Gary Bettman said in a statement. "Such contact between any National Hockey League personnel - coaches, players, league officials or team executives - and media personnel will not be tolerated.
"We want a clear message sent to the media who cover our games that they have a safe environment in which to work."
Bettman met with Hasek on Thursday to discuss the incident.

"Mr. Hasek has expressed his regret to me over the incident," Bettman said. "He has also apologised to Mr. Kelley and the Buffalo News. Mr. Hasek also apologises to his team and to the fans of the Sabres and of hockey.
Hasek, a leading contender for the Hart Trophy as league MVP, will be allowed to practice and travel with the team. He will be eligible to play in Game 4 on May 9.
